events.title: Vatican I's constitution Dei Filius
events.shortBlurb: The First Vatican Council defined the harmony of faith and reason against the errors of the age…
body: On 24 April 1870, the First Vatican Council solemnly approved the Dogmatic Constitution Dei Filius, on the Catholic faith. Meeting under Pope Pius IX, the council addressed the rationalism, materialism, and doubt of the nineteenth century.

The constitution taught that God can be known with certainty by the natural light of human reason from created things, and that faith and reason, both gifts of the one God, can never truly contradict one another. It set out the Church's teaching on revelation, faith, and the relation of the two.

Dei Filius was one of the two great constitutions of the council, the other, Pastor Aeternus, defining the primacy and infallibility of the pope, before the council was cut short by the outbreak of war.
